UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                    BEFORE THE
                       FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

Midcontinent Independent System Operator                 )             Docket No. ER26-3813-000

                                MOTION TO INTERVENE AND
                        INITIAL COMMENTS OF RWE AMERICAS, LLC

            Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“FERC”

or the “Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedures,1 and the Commission’s September 22,

2026 Notice regarding the Midwestern Interconnection Transmission Operator’s (“MISO”)

legacy queue acceleration proposal filed on September 21, 2026 in the above captioned

proceeding, RWE Americas, LLC (“RWEA”) respectfully submits this Motion to Intervene and

Comments.

      I.       COMMUNICATIONS

            Communications with respect to this matter should be addressed to:

                   Paul Varnado                   Eric Stephens
                   Assistant General Counsel      Sr. Dir., Regulatory Affairs Wholesale Markets
                   RWE Americas, LLC              RWE Americas, LLC
                   353 N. Clark St., 30th Floor   353 N. Clark St., 30th Floor
                   Chicago, IL 60654              Chicago, IL 60654
                   Tel: (312) 358-9873            Tel: (872) 378-7101
                   paul.varnado@rwe.com           eric.stephens@rwe.com

      II.      MOTION TO INTERVENE

            RWEA is a Delaware limited liability company which, through various affiliated and

subsidiary project companies, is in the business of developing, owning, and operating wholesale

electric generation and energy storage facilities throughout the United States. RWEA owns and

operates a renewable energy portfolio of approximately 12 gigawatts installed capacity of




1
    18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212, and 385.214.
                                                     1
 onshore wind, solar, and battery storage in the United States, and is an indirect wholly-owned

subsidiary of RWE AG, a German company.

             Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure,

RWEA hereby moves to intervene in this proceeding.2 RWEA is the developer, owner, and

operator of generation resources that would be impacted by the proposed queue reform as

contemplated in MISO’s legacy queue acceleration proposal. RWEA has an interest in ensuring

that MISO’s proposed queue reform achieves the stated goals and does not result in undue

negative impact upon RWEA owned projects and interconnection customers or the MISO grid

that serves them. As such, RWEA has a material interest in the outcome of this proceeding that

cannot be adequately represented by any other party. RWEA respectfully requests that the

Commission grant it full rights associated with party status in this proceeding.

      III.      COMMENTS OF RWE AMERICAS, LLC

             RWE Americas, LLC respectfully submits these comments regarding the filing by the

Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. to revise its Generator Interconnection

Procedures to address legacy interconnection queue delays, particularly those associated with the

Definitive Planning Phase (“DPP”) 2022 cycle. MISO proposes, among other reforms, a one-

time opportunity for penalty-free withdrawal for DPP-2022 participants, increased post-Decision

Point II withdrawal thresholds, and a limit of one Phase III restudy for all Definitive Planning

Process ("DPP") cycles.

             RWEA appreciates the considerable effort undertaken by MISO and stakeholders to

develop this proposal addressing ways to reliably and efficiently process projects more quickly

through the interconnection queue. RWEA supports the objective of the filing: more efficient



2
    18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212 and 385.214.
                                                    2
 processing of the interconnection queue. At the same time, RWEA believes additional reforms

are needed if MISO is to fully achieve the Commission's goals of increased certainty, reduced

speculation, and timely interconnection of generation resources. This filing offers a first step, but

more is needed.

       While MISO's proposal addresses study timing risk, it does not adequately address a

second, equally important challenge: the continuing exposure of projects that have executed

Generation Interconnection Agreements ("GIAs") to significant and potentially unpredictable

cost reallocations resulting from subsequent project withdrawals. As discussed below, the

Commission should approve MISO's proposal while encouraging MISO and stakeholders

quickly to develop additional tariff reforms that provide greater cost certainty for projects that

have demonstrated commercial readiness and executed GIAs. As an interim measure, MISO

should clarify on the record in this case that it will detail in stakeholder discussions and its

Business Practices Manual the process it will use that will ensure developers are not subject to

unnecessary upgrades after its final proposed re-study.

           1. RWEA Supports Aspects of MISO's Proposal

       RWEA agrees with MISO's position that unlimited post-Phase III restudies have become

a major obstacle to efficient queue administration. MISO documents how earlier queue cycles

have experienced repeated withdrawals and numerous restudies, resulting in extensive delays and

prolonged uncertainty for projects that remain viable and ready to proceed. MISO points to the

fact that in the DPP-2019 Central region alone, nine restudies and four study report revisions

occurred following issuance of the initial Final System Impact Study, significantly extending the

timeline for project advancement.




                                                   3
           The DPP-2022 cycle presents even greater risks. As MISO explains, DPP-2022 began

with approximately 911 interconnection requests representing roughly 161 GW of generation

and remains the largest cycle in MISO history. Even after substantial attrition, hundreds of

projects remain under study. Without additional safeguards, the probability of cascading

withdrawals and repeated re-studies is substantial.

          Accordingly, RWEA supports:

   •      The one-time penalty-free withdrawal opportunity available before Decision Point II for

          DPP-2022 participants.

   •      The establishment of a defined Phase III conclusion process.

   •      A limitation on post-Phase III restudies.

          Collectively, these reforms represent an improvement over the status quo and should help

ensure that DPP-2022 can be completed without the extensive delays experienced in prior legacy

cycles.

             2. Additional Reforms Are Needed to Provide Greater Cost Certainty

          Although RWEA supports aspects of the filing, MISO’s proposal focuses primarily on

limiting study delays and does not sufficiently address the continuing uncertainty associated with

network upgrade cost allocations after projects have executed GIAs.

          To bring speed to power, a critical goal shared across the industry not only for large

loads, but for all new generation, schedule and cost certainty are equally important. A project

that reaches GIA execution has typically committed substantial development capital, secured

land rights, obtained permits, advanced equipment procurement plans, and arranged financing.

Yet that project may still face significant future exposure if later withdrawals trigger cost

reallocations associated with shared network upgrades. As a result, commercially mature projects



                                                      4
 remain exposed to risks that can undermine financing assumptions and project viability long

after they have demonstrated their commitment to proceed.

       RWEA therefore respectfully submits that MISO should clarify on the record in this

docket that it will detail in stakeholder discussions and its Business Practices Manual the process

it will use that will ensure developers are not subject to unnecessary upgrades after its final

proposed re-study. Moreover, MISO’s proposal should be viewed as a one of many needed steps

rather than the final solution to Phase III uncertainty.

           3. RWEA Recommends a Two-Restudy Framework

       RWEA suggests as part of its continuous queue improvement initiatives and to provide

greater clarity, MISO promptly initiate stakeholder discussions to implement a framework that

would limit Phase III studies to no more than two formal restudies. Under this approach, a first

re-study would remove projects that withdraw at or before the completion of Decision Point III

and prior to GIA execution. A second and final re-study would remove projects that elect not to

execute GIAs. After completion of the second restudy, study results and network upgrade

assignments would become effectively final except as necessary to address reliability concerns

associated with specific withdrawn projects.

       This framework would achieve several objectives:

   •   Provide developers and lenders greater confidence in final upgrade obligations.

   •   Allow MISO to account for the most significant attrition events that traditionally occur

       before GIA execution.

   •   Establish a clear endpoint beyond which projects can rely on study outcomes for

       financing and construction decisions.

   •   Reduce incentives for strategic delay behaviors.



                                                   5
 Importantly, the two-restudy framework would still improve upon the existing process while

offering materially greater certainty than a single-restudy construct.

           4. Security Requirements Should Be Used to Support Cost Certainty

       RWEA also recommends that MISO include, in stakeholder discussions supporting

continuous queue improvement, consideration of a change that more closely aligns financial

security requirements with the objective of preserving network upgrade cost certainty.

Specifically, following completion of DPP Phase III, developers should post security covering

100 percent of allocated Interconnection Facilities and Network Upgrade obligations. The

required security would subsequently be adjusted following completion of the final authorized

restudy process. Once a project executes its GIA, the security associated with shared network

upgrades should become fully at risk.

       This approach would accomplish two important goals. First, it would ensure that projects

remaining in the queue have demonstrated a meaningful financial commitment to move forward.

Second, it would provide a dedicated funding source for shared network upgrades if later

withdrawals occur. Such a framework better aligns commercial incentives and places the

financial consequences of withdrawal on the projects that create those impacts rather than solely

on the projects that remain committed to construction.

           5. Post-Final-Restudy Withdrawals Should Not Trigger Full-Cycle Restudies

       Once the final authorized restudy is complete, subsequent withdrawals should not trigger

another broad cycle-wide restudy. Instead, MISO should conduct a narrowly tailored review

focused solely on determining whether a withdrawn project's associated network upgrades

remain necessary. If the review determines that a network upgrade remains required, then the




                                                 6
 withdrawing project's posted security should remain available to support construction of that

upgrade.

          Conversely, if the review determines that the upgrade is no longer required, the security

associated with that upgrade should be returned to remaining participants that share

responsibility for the facility. This targeted approach would preserve reliability while avoiding

the administrative burden, delay, and uncertainty associated with additional cycle-wide studies.

             6. The Commission Should Encourage Application to DPP-2022

          RWEA would note that these provisions, to the extent practicable, should be applied to

DPP-2022 and also to future DPP cycles in order to provide the necessary timing and cost

certainty needed to facilitate more rapid processing of projects in the queue. The Commission

has repeatedly emphasized the need to reduce uncertainty and facilitate timely development of

new generation resources. Further collaboration and proactive steps today will help to ensure that

the durable reforms RWEA has suggested are in place before similar challenges emerge in future

cycles.

   IV.       Conclusion

          RWEA respectfully requests that the Commission:

             1. Approve MISO's proposed tariff revisions, as commented on herein.

             2. Recognize the substantial benefits associated with limiting Phase III restudies and

                  providing a defined endpoint for legacy queue processing.

             3. Encourage MISO and stakeholders to develop additional tariff reforms focused on

                  cost certainty for projects that execute GIAs as expeditiously as possible.

             4.   Encourage MISO to promptly pursue reforms that:

                     o   Limit formal Phase III restudies to two defined restudies;



                                                   7
               o   Require full security posting for network upgrades and interconnection

                  facilities;

              o   Place withdrawal risk on withdrawing projects through at-risk security

                  mechanisms; and

              o   Restrict post-final-restudy reviews to targeted analyses of affected

                  network upgrades rather than broad cycle-wide restudies.

       5. Encourage timely implementation of these additional reforms, including

          application to the DPP-2022 cycle where practicable and then to future DPP

          cycles as well to prevent a recurrence of some of the issues that have made DPP-

          2022 a significant challenge for MISO and stakeholders.

                                         Respectfully submitted,

                                         /s/ Eric Stephens
                                         RWE Americas, LLC




Dated: October 5, 2026
